title: POC deployment pathfinder — FinServ options and recommended hybrid approach
content:
Summary:
This note captures the decisions and recommended architecture options from the Feb 11 FinServ POC workshop. Customer constraints: strict data residency (EU only), mandatory HSM-backed key management, audit retention for 7 years, sub-200ms 95th percentile latency for query path, and throughput up to 150 qps for text generation endpoints during business hours. The objective of the POC is to validate correctness (privacy and auditability), latency SLOs, and an operational runbook for a hybrid deployment that balances time-to-PoC and long-term compliance needs.

High-level recommendation (short):
Run a hybrid deployment: Redwood hosted control plane + private inference runtime in the customer's EU VPC. For the POC, use a small dedicated GPU pool in the customer VPC (Dedicated mode) with automatic fallback to a hosted non-sensitive model variant for degraded capacity. This provides a fast path to validate latency and audit while meeting KMS/HSM and data residency constraints.

Why hybrid for FinServ POC (rationale):
- Compliance: Customer requires KMS/HSM integration and physical control over inference logs. Private runtime in their VPC lets them attach their HSM and route logs into their SIEM.
- Latency and throughput control: Dedicated GPUs in-customer enable predictable tail latency for the 95th percentile target.
- Operational velocity: Hosted control plane accelerates onboarding (token issuance, model catalog), reduces engineering effort for initial rollout.
- Graceful degradation: Hosted fallback avoids complete outage during capacity or software issues while still preserving non-sensitive functionality.

Architectural options considered (short list):
1) Fully hosted (control + runtime in Redwood clouds): fastest to stand up, worst for compliance/residency.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity in Redwood datacenter in EU): good predictable performance, better data isolation but cust still sends data off-prem.
3) Private (customer-managed runtime in VPC / on-prem): strongest compliance and residency, higher setup time.
4) Hybrid (hosted control plane + VPC runtime + fallback to hosted runtime): balances speed and compliance — recommended.

Detailed POC design (hybrid):
- Control plane: Redwood hosted API for access management, telemetry ingestion (only metadata, configurable). Customer opts-in to telemetry types; raw request/response payloads are never stored in hosted analytics unless explicitly allowed.
- Runtime: Customer-deployed Redwood runtime in EU VPC, provisioned with a small Dedicated GPU pool (2x A10 equivalent nodes) for the POC. Runtime configured for local KMS/HSM via CloudHSM or vendor HSM connector.
- Networking: Private subnets for inference pods, NAT egress only to Redwood control plane endpoints for heartbeats and model version metadata. Inbound access from customer application through internal load balancer.
- Logging: All request/response payloads retained in customer-managed blob storage with lifecycle policies. Redwood runtime sends structured audit records (sha256 of request) to the hosted control plane for correlation only.
- Model variants & fallback: Primary: quantized, customer-approved open model hosted in VPC. Fallback: hosted curvature-tuned model variant with redacted contexts for non-sensitive requests. Automatic fallback policies configurable by route.

Security and compliance specifics for POC:
- KMS/HSM: Customer will provide HSM endpoints and credentials; runtime must support PKCS#11 or cloud HSM connectors. Key wrapping for model encryption required.
- Network isolation: No public IPs on inference nodes; egress restricted via proxy and allowlist to Redwood control plane.
- Audit: Immutable append-only audit log (signed entries) stored in customer AWS S3 (or equivalent) with server-side encryption and MFK policies.
- Data residency: All model weights and cache artifacts stored in EU-only storage with encryption at rest.
- Pen-testing: POC includes a scoped threat model and pre-production pentest run after the first week of traffic.

Performance plan and acceptance criteria (POC success metrics):
- Latency: 95th percentile < 200ms for the default prompt shape (avg 50 tokens) under 150 qps burst.
- Throughput: sustained 120 qps with 10% CPU/GPU headroom.
- Cost: Beta estimate shows per-token cost on Dedicated VPC ~1.6x higher than hosted due to small pool inefficiencies; aim to validate batching improvements.
- Correctness: 100% of sampled requests must have traceable audit records, and any PII redaction rules must pass the automated tests.
- Reliability: Runtime must survive a simulated instance failure with no more than 5s error surface to the application (fallback path).

POC scope and timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0: Kickoff, access provisioning, KMS/HSM credential exchange, network peering plan.
- Week 1: Runtime deploy template (Terraform) into test VPC; bootstrap model download and cache warmup.
- Weeks 2–3: Load test + observability integration (console hooks, SLO dashboards), implement fallback policy.
- Week 4: Compliance checks, audit log verification, pentest smoke.
- Week 5: Production-like rehearsal with synthetic traffic and failover drills.
- Week 6: Review, handoff to customer ops, extension recommendation.

Operational runbook highlights (for deployment run by SE):
- Pre-deploy checklist: VPC subnets, HSM endpoints, IAM role for runtime, S3 audit bucket with kms key ARN, internal LB DNS.
- Deployment steps: terraform apply -> runtime bootstrap -> model pull -> healthcheck/trace sampling -> warm traffic.
- Failure modes: GPU OOM -> fallback to smaller batch size; node loss -> autoscaler replaces node within configured cooldown; control plane disconnect -> runtime switches to cached policy and continues serving.
- Escalation: If audit logs stop flowing, immediate alert to SE on-call and customer security lead; freeze model rollout until investigation completes.

Evaluation harness and tests (deliverables):
- Traffic replay tool with obfuscated PII; latency and correctness measurement scripts.
- Prompt-set for quality/regression testing with ground-truth expected outputs and scoring.
- Audit verification script that replays log entries and validates signing, order, and retention rules.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Slow HSM crypto operations causing latency spikes. Mitigation: local HSM caching of unwrap keys and async tagging, run microbenchmarks early.
- Risk: Customer network egress policies blocking control plane heartbeats. Mitigation: pre-approved allowlist and testing during Week 1.
- Risk: Model footprint too large for target nodes. Mitigation: test quantized variants and multi-model sharding.

Open questions for customer (to resolve before Week 1):
- Which HSM vendor and protocol (PKCS#11, CloudHSM)?
- Acceptable telemetry scope to send to Redwood hosted control plane?
- SLA expectations post-POC for Dedicated pool size and support window.

Action items (owners):
- Maya: Draft Terraform runtime template and deployment runbook (due Feb 18).
- Arjun: Prepare load-test scripts and initial perf expectations (due Feb 20).
- Lucas: Coordinate HSM integration test and sample configs (due Feb 21).
- Customer Security: Provide HSM endpoints and allowlisted egress IPs (due Feb 16).

Appendix — quick cost sketch (ballpark for POC month):
- Dedicated VPC runtime (2 A10-class nodes) + storage + egress: estimated $12k–18k/month.
- Redwood support and onboarding hours (SE): 40–80 hours depending on handoff: $12k–24k one-time.
- Note: costs expected to drop with pooling and batching in production.

Notes and record of workshop decisions: 
- Team consensus: Hybrid approach is the most pragmatic for this customer.
- Customer requested a single sign-off checkpoint after Week 3 to re-evaluate ongoing Dedicated commitment.
- Next sync scheduled Feb 17 to review Terraform template and run first perf smoke.

End of document.
